items.actClause:
AN ACT to amend the administrative code of the city of New York, in relation
to the exclusion of certain grants as taxable income for certain business
taxes, the imposition of the business corporation tax, the credit of certain
overpayments of tax against other taxes owed, and the disclosure of owners of
limited liability companies with respect to the real property transfer tax; to
amend the tax law, in relation to a city pass-through entity tax; and to amend
chapter 59 of the laws of 2022, relating to a city pass-through entity tax, in
relation to the city pass-through entity tax
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S9454

SPONSOR: KRUEGER
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the administrative code of the city of New York, in
relation to the exclusion of certain grants as taxable income for
certain business taxes, the imposition of the business corporation tax,
the credit of certain overpayments of tax against other taxes owed, and
the disclosure of owners of limited liability companies with respect to
the real property transfer tax; to amend the tax law, in relation to a
city pass-through entity tax; and to amend chapter 59 of the laws of
2022, relating to a city pass-through entity tax, in relation to the
city pass-through entity tax

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Sections 1, 3, 4, and 5 of the bill add new provisions to subdivision
(c) of section 11-506 relating to the unincorporated business tax
("UBT"), subdivision 8 of section 11-602 relating to the general corpo-
ration tax, section 11-641 relating to the banking corporation tax, and
subdivision 8 of section 11-652 relating to the corporate tax of 2015,
respectively. The amendments provide that, for the purposes of calculat-
ing entire net income for each such tax, a taxpayer should not include
any grants received through the New York State COVID-19 Pandemic Small
Business Recovery Grant Program or the City's Small Business Resilience
Grant Program.

Section 2 of the bill amends subdivision a of section 11-526 of the
Administrative Code of the City of New York to provide that the New York
City Commissioner of Finance may credit any overpayment of the UBT
against any tax liability the taxpayer has for any other City tax that
has been imposed pursuant to title 11 of the Administrative Code.
Section 2 also provides that this credit of the overpayment against
other City taxes shall be applied before any part of such overpayment is
paid to the State Commissioner of Taxation and Finance, as described in
section 171-m of the Tax Law.

Section 6 of the bill amends subparagraph (3) of paragraph (b) of subdi-
vision 8 of section 11-652 of the Administrative Code to provide that
the entire net income, for purposes of computing the City's corporate
tax of 2015, otherwise known as the business corporation tax, be deter-
mined without the exclusion, deduction or credit of any New York taxes
that are based on income or profit, including taxes paid or accrued
pursuant to article 24-A or 24-B of the Tax Law.

Section 7 of the bill amends paragraphs (a), (b), and (d) of subdivision
1 of section 11-653 of the Administrative Code to provide that corpo-
rations deriving receipts from City sources of $1 million or more be
subject to the City's business corporation tax. A corporation with less
than $1 million but more than $10,000 of receipts from City sources will
also be subject to the City's business corporation tax if the corpo-
ration is part of a unitary group that in the aggregate derives receipts
from City sources of $1 million or more.

Currently, paragraph (c) of this subdivision provides that a corporation
is doing business in the City if for the taxable year:  (1) the corpo-
ration has a total of 1,000 or more credit card customers who have a
mailing address within the City; (2) the corporation has merchant
customer contracts amounting to 1,000 or more locations; or (3) the sum
of such customers and locations amounts to 1,000 or more. The amendments
to paragraph (d) of this subdivision provide that a corporation that is
part of a unitary group which in the aggregate meets the three require-
ments of paragraph (c) is doing business in the City if the corporation
has at least ten such customers or locations, or at least ten customers
and locations.

Section 7 of the bill also amends subdivisions 2 and 2-a of section
11-653 of the Administrative Code so that foreign and alien corpo-
rations, respectively, will not be deemed to be deriving receipts from
City sources if they meet the same criteria currently used to determine
that they are not doing business, employing capital, owning or leasing
property, or maintaining an office in the City.

Section 8 of the bill amends subdivision 1 of section 11-677 of the
Administrative Code to provide that the City Commissioner of Finance may
credit any overpayment of any tax imposed pursuant to chapter 6 of title
11 of the Administrative Code against any tax liability the taxpayer has
for any other City tax that has been imposed pursuant to title 11 of the
Administrative Code. Section 8 also provides that this credit of the
overpayment against other City taxes shall be applied before any part of
such overpayment is paid to the State Commissioner of Taxation and
Finance, as described in section 171-m of the Tax Law.

Section 9 of the bill amends subdivision (h) of section 11-2105 of the
Administrative Code to make clear that the reporting requirements for
limited liability companies that are grantors or grantees of deeds for
certain residential real properties are applicable to buildings used as
residential real property that contain up to 4 family dwelling units.
However, these reporting requirements do not apply to a member, manager,
or authorized person of such limited liability company if the member,
manager, or authorized person is a publicly traded entity, a REIT, an
UPREIT, or a mutual fund.

Section 10 of the bill provides that this bill takes effect immediately,
except that sections 1, 3, 4, and 5 of the bill shall be retroactive to
and deemed to have been in full force and effect for tax years beginning
on or after January I, 2021, and sections 6 and 7 of the bill shall be
applicable to tax years beginning on or after January 1, 2022.

 
REASONS FOR SUPPORT:

This bill aligns certain tax-related provisions of the Administrative
Code to each other and to the Tax Law.

First, the bill excludes grant amounts that small businesses in the City
received from the New York State COVID-19 Small Business Recovery Grant
Program or the City's Small Business Resilience Grant Program from
calculation of entire net income for the City's local business income
taxes, in the same manner the State grants have been excluded from taxa-
tion under the state corporate taxes and personal income taxes. In 2021,
the Legislature excluded the State COVID-19 Small Business Recovery
Grants from the calculation of income for the state corporate tax and
the personal income tax but did not enact similar exclusions for these
grants from the City's business income taxes. See L. 2021, Ch. 157. The
bill rectifies that omission and conforms the calculation of income for
the City's business taxes with that for the State taxes. The bill simi-
larly excludes from the calculation of entire net income for the City's
business taxes, grants received as part of the City's Small Business
Resilience Grant Program.

Second, in light of recent state legislation, certain tax provisions of
the Administrative Code must now be conformed to each other. As part of
the 2022-2023 State budget, the Legislature amended the Administrative
Code so that any tax that the State or any subdivision of the State may
impose, including any tax paid as a result of a taxpayer's election to
pay tax under the State or City pass-through entity tax, imposed by
articles 24-A or 24-B of the Tax Law, would not reduce the taxpayer's
taxable income for the purposes of calculating the City's general corpo-
ration tax or banking corporation tax. See L. 2022, ch. 59, part MM,
subpart B, §§ 9-10. This bill makes a similar change to section 11-652
of the Administrative Code, so that a taxpayer's payment of any other
tax on income imposed by the State or any subdivision of the State will
not negatively affect the calculation of business corporation tax
liability.

Third, the bill further conforms the State and City business corporation
taxes to each other. Both the State and the City corporate tax laws were
amended in 2014 and 2015, respectively, so that the allocation of a
taxpayer's business income is consistent with the concept of customer-
based sourcing. See L. 2014, ch. 59, part A; L. 2015, ch. 60, part D.
This concept means a taxpayer's income is taxed on the taxpayer's
economic activity within a jurisdiction in addition to the traditional
standard of being taxed based on the taxpayer's physical presence in a
jurisdiction. Although an economic nexus concept was included in the
State's business corporation tax reform in 2014, identical economic
nexus provisions were not included when the City's corporate tax reform
was enacted in 2015. As a result, the City's business corporation tax is
both out of step with the State's on this issue and is internally incon-
sistent.  This bill will fix this discrepancy, using the same economic
nexus threshold levels that already exist for the State corporate tax
and applying them to the City.

Fourth, the bill conforms provisions on certain limited liability compa-
ny reporting requirements in the Tax Law and the Administrative Code. In
2019, the Legislature added the same requirements to both the Tax Law
and the Administrative Code in the same act. See L. 2019, ch. 297. In
2021, the Legislature made clarifying amendments to the Tax Law, but at
that time did not make the same changes to the Administrative Code
provisions. See L. 2021, ch. 59, part 0, § 3.  Those amendments are now
made in this bill.

Finally, the bill conforms provisions on the overpayments of taxes in
the Tax Law and Administrative Code. Current law unduly restricts the
ability of the City Finance Commissioner to credit overpayments of tax.
Section 11-526 of the Administrative Code allows overpayments of UBT to
be credited against only other UBT liabilities and for business and
income taxes imposed under chapters 6, 17 and 19 of title 11 of the
Administrative Code. Similarly, section 11-677 of the Administrative
Code allows overpayments of business taxes imposed by chapter 6 of title
11 of the Administrative Code to be credited against only the liabil-
ities of other such taxes. Notably, neither Administrative Code section
authorizes overpayment of UBT or of a chapter 6 business tax to be cred-
ited against other New York City taxes, including excise taxes. By
contrast, section 1086 of Tax Law, which governs overpayments of certain
State corporate taxes, authorizes the State Commissioner of Taxation and
Finance to credit an overpayment of State corporate tax against any tax
liability for any tax imposed under the Tax Law, including sales taxes
and excise taxes. This bill will fix this incongruity by granting the
City Finance Commissioner more authority to credit UBT and business tax
overpayments.

Accordingly, the Mayor urges the earliest possible favorable consider-
ation of this proposal by the Legislature.

summary: Relates to the exclusion of certain grants as taxable income for certain business taxes, the imposition of the business corporation tax, the credit of certain overpayments of tax against other taxes owed, and the disclosure of owners of limited liability companies with respect to the real property transfer tax; relates to a city pass-through entity tax.
